label: The third factor differs from the matching normative truth in at most an e2 share of cases
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise for #1586, attribution deferred. On the same distribution, the survival/goods factor F differs from the normative truth M about the same acts, under one fixed verdict type, in a set of cases of measure at most e2. A small e2 is what a two-sided third-factor correlation needs. His premise that survival is pro tanto good does not bound it for all-things-considered or impartial verdicts, nor the reverse direction of the pro tanto gap (cases where F fails and a pro tanto reason holds anyway); at most it bears on the cases where F holds and no reason does, and even that part only qualifiedly, since survival is not always good. No value of e2 is supplied, and its normative and empirical calibration is open.
